players.product: MachXO5-NX control FPGAs and Mach-NX / MachXO3D hardware root-of-trust (PFR) FPGAs on server boards

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Lattice's AI penetration (some on the data path, some in the server domain; 'We don't do very much direct AI compute') has 'grown into the high 20% of our overall business, which means it's a greater percent of the compute business.' Server attach rate: 'five, four years ago, it was 1.x, then it went to 2.x. Now it's 3.x, and it's now even higher', with 'up to 100 attach points or even greater than that in an AI server rack'; ASPs are expanding as customers move from MachXO2 / MachXO3 / MachXO3D to MachXO5 and some Nexus parts. New attach comes from manageability (power and cooling) and leak detection, which '18 months ago nobody thought about... now is a really critical application'. CFO view: over three to five years unit volume growth from more attach points stays the primary FPGA driver, with ASPs secondary; FPGA content is insulated from ASIC replacement because 'You don't want to spend two nanometer silicon... on I/O expansion. Makes way more sense to do it in a 65 nanometer FPGA', and rack design cycles are shortening 'from two years to 18 months to 12 months'.
quarterly_data.figure: AI in the high 20% of overall business; attach rate 3.x and higher; up to 100 attach points per AI server rack

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the FPGA business: 'We had about a $500 million a year business last year. We'll end the year approximately double that in the FPGA side, and we expect to continue to grow next year. That means our supply chain has to be 2x plus more robust, and that's what we're driving to.' He said the growth is 'not temporary'.
quarterly_data.figure: FPGA business about $500 million last year; approximately double that this year; supply chain 2x plus

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on supply and visibility: as demand rose earlier this year lead times increased, 'in some cases it got over a year', and have been managed 'back down to the in the 40s'. 'The pinch point is assembly test or packaging'; the fab side is comfortable because Lattice uses older nodes; Lattice has 'invested a lot in... tester capacity, for the final test and ship out to the customer' (visible in its capex) and is expanding its supply chain. Its book 'has continued to grow in total dollar value and then expand out in time', and channel inventory has been tightened. Confirming visibility to the end of 2027: 'we have bookings out through Q4 of next year. We are not booked out in the sense that we can't support more demand. We can support more demand.'
quarterly_data.figure: lead times over a year at peak, now in the 40s; bookings out through Q4 of next year

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on physical AI: Lattice is strong in sensor fusion and vision ('Multiple cameras coming into one stream with some pre-processing and that's part of the Holoscan platform from NVIDIA that we're on'); 'We think we have a footprint in almost all of the robotics companies' and is enabling 'a more software-like programming environment' for FPGAs. On volume timing: 'We're not sure. We'll probably start seeing it in the end of next year', with 'multiple sockets per instance'. The core industrial business (mostly traditional factory automation) is recovering: 'year-on-year, let's call it 20% growth in industrial from last year, and we think that will grow again next year'; little automotive exposure.
quarterly_data.figure: industrial up about 20% year-on-year; physical AI volume probably from the end of next year
